Visit note | 2025-06-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Bushra Akter, 79, female. Mrs. Akter returns for a follow-up visit regarding her cardiovascular symptoms. Instead of classic chest heaviness, she describes experiencing jaw and left arm discomfort on effort with no chest pain, which is accompanied by breathlessness on exertion. She works as a farmer and notes that these episodes originally started while carrying shopping bags uphill in Tejgaon. She denies experiencing dizzy spells, ankle swelling, or palpitations at rest. On physical examination, her vital signs are BP 150/96 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and weight 59 kg. Her chest is clear on auscultation, and her heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-06-15 04:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Shahana Matubbar, 55, female. This patient presents for her first visit complaining of high fever, a productive cough yielding yellow or green sputum, and a sharp chest pain when she breathes in deeply. Her symptoms began a week after a flu-like illness in Khilgaon. She works as a sales representative, which requires significant travel. She denies any leg swelling, night sweats, or hemoptysis. Clinical examination reveals a temperature 102.1°F, BP 121/72 mmHg, pulse 99 bpm, SpO2 95%, and weight 51 kg. Bronchial breath sounds and crackles are audible in the right lower lung field. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She has been advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and she must return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 09:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Mahbub Faruque, 54, male. Mr. Faruque presents for an initial consultation, reporting that he experiences a tight feeling in his chest when walking quickly or climbing stairs, along with breathlessness on effort. He is a cricket coach and first noticed these symptoms while climbing to a fourth-floor flat in Savar. He denies any chest pain at rest, lightheadedness, or orthopnea. On examination, his vitals are BP 155/89 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, and weight 76 kg. Heart sounds are normal with no murmurs, and lung fields are clear. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up is scheduled in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 09:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Habiba Sarkar, 52, female. Mrs. Sarkar presents with complaints of heat intolerance, a racing heart, and tremors in her hands. She works as a restaurant cook and first noticed these symptoms when her clothes became loose during a stay in Sirajganj. She has no history of neck swelling, visual changes, or loose stools. On physical examination, she has a pulse 118 bpm, BP 128/78 mmHg, and weight 67 kg. A fine tremor is visible when her hands are outstretched, and there is no palpable goitre. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and to rest when the heart races. Follow-up is scheduled in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 09:00 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Arifa Sheikh, 43, female. Mrs. Sheikh returns for a follow-up, presenting with stiffness in both shoulders at the same time, which has left her unable to reach behind her back for several weeks. She works as a shopkeeper and reports that the trouble began after a minor fall at home in Old Dhaka. She denies any numbness or tingling in her arms. On examination, her shoulder lifts only to 70 degrees in active abduction, with a similar restriction in passive range of motion. Her other vitals are BP 132/70 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, and weight 56 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 10:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sumitra Roy, 54, female. Mrs. Roy presents for a follow-up review of her metabolic health. She had been experiencing frequent urination and unintentional weight loss. She is a software developer and notes that her elevated blood sugar was first found during a routine test before a trip to Motijheel. She denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or numbness in her extremities. On examination, her fasting glucose 11.6 mmol/L, BP 126/72 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 79 kg. Foot sensation is intact to monofilament testing. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check her feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 10:00 AM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Sadia Bepari, 43, female. Mrs. Bepari returns for a follow-up regarding her nasal allergies, complaining of itchy eyes and congestion that is significantly worse with dust exposure. Working as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver, she reports her symptoms have become worse since road construction began near her home in Kushtia. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any facial pain, fever, or purulent nasal discharge. On examination, she experiences about 4 sneezing fits a day. Her other vitals are BP 119/70 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, and weight 58 kg. Nasal turbinates are pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash her bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 10:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Sabina Gazi, 28, female. Mrs. Gazi presents for a follow-up visit regarding her hormonal symptoms, reporting weight gain, facial hirsutism, and acne. She is a pharmacist and noticed the weight gain after starting a desk job in Banani. She has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. She denies any voice deepening or rapid hair loss. On examination, her BMI 25.0, BP 143/86 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, and weight 54 kg. Mild facial acne and hirsutism are noted. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 10:30 AM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Faruk Matubbar, 30, male. Mr. Matubbar presents for his first visit complaining of bloating and stools that switch between loose and hard, with symptoms significantly worsening during periods of stress. He works as a security guard, and these bowel changes first began after a bout of food poisoning in Badda. His medical history includes a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies any rectal bleeding, unexplained weight loss, or nocturnal diarrhea. On examination, he reports a pain score 3/10. His other vitals are BP 146/92 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, and weight 56 kg. Abdomen is soft and mildly tender in the left lower quadrant. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce his intake of tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 10:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Nirmal Sen, 78, male. Mr. Sen returns for a follow-up, reporting persistent burning in both feet that becomes much worse at night. He is a farmer and first noticed these symptoms after long hours standing at a factory in Noakhali. He denies any weakness in his legs, back pain, or difficulty walking. Physical examination reveals reduced sensation at 3 of 10 monofilament test sites. His other vitals are BP 127/81 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, and weight 91 kg. Lower limb reflexes are slightly diminished bilaterally. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep his blood sugar under control. Follow-up is in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 11:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Jubayer Shikder, 66, male. Mr. Shikder presents for his first visit with a flare-up of respiratory symptoms, reporting wheezing on walking, an increased amount of sputum compared to his usual baseline, and a long history of smoking. He is currently a homemaker, and his breathing flared after rubbish was burned near his home in Chattogram. He denies chest pain, high fever, or hemoptysis. On examination, his oxygen saturation is SpO2 90%, BP 127/71 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 65 kg. Diffuse expiratory wheezing is heard throughout both lung fields. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 week, or sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 11:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Rahima Matubbar, 19, female. This young patient presents for an initial assessment, complaining of constant worry for several months, feeling restless, and poor sleep. She works as a garment factory worker and reports that her anxiety has become significantly worse since experiencing job insecurity at her company in Mohammadpur. She denies any panic attacks, suicidal ideation, or hallucinations. Mental status examination shows a GAD-7 score 12. Her other physical vitals are BP 118/74 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, and weight 74 kg. She appears anxious but is cooperative and well-oriented. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 12:00 PM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Krishna Das, 69, female. Mrs. Das returns for a follow-up evaluation of her thyroid function. She describes feeling slow and tired, and always feeling unusually cold. She works as a madrasa teacher and first noticed these symptoms when a cold winter in Keraniganj felt much harder to tolerate than usual. She denies any neck pain, voice changes, or constipation. On examination, her TSH 15.8 mIU/L, BP 116/85 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 79 kg. No thyroid enlargement or peripheral edema is noted. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-06-16 03:30 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Champa Shikder, 32, female. Mrs. Shikder is seen for a follow-up visit regarding her hormonal symptoms, complaining of acne and weight gain. She is a homemaker and first noticed these changes after a friend in Cox's Bazar suggested she get tested. She denies any abnormal hair loss, severe pelvic pain, or voice changes. On examination, her BMI 30.1, BP 128/70 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 55 kg. Mild facial acne is present. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 10:30 AM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Sabina Bhuiyan, 45, female. Mrs. Bhuiyan presents for an initial consultation, complaining of a persistent runny nose and nasal symptoms that worsen significantly with dust. She works as a garment merchandiser and reports that her condition has been worse since she began keeping a cat at home in Bogura. She denies any sore throat, fever, or facial pressure. On examination, she experiences about 10 sneezing fits a day. Her other vitals are BP 124/85 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, and weight 45 kg. The nasal mucosa appears pale and swollen. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash her bedding weekly. Follow-up is in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 11:30 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Sanjida Begum, 28, female. Ms. Begum presents for her first visit with swelling of the eyelid and a painful red lump at the edge of her eyelid. She is a textile engineer and mentions that this lesion appeared during a stressful week in Rangpur. Her medical history includes a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She denies any visual changes, double vision, or discharge from the eye. On examination, there is a lump about 5 mm on the right upper eyelid that is erythematous and tender to touch. Other vitals are BP 132/81 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, and weight 86 kg. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, not squeeze the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Laila Talukder, 52, female. Mrs. Talukder presents for her first visit complaining of producing more sputum than usual and breathlessness that has been worse for several days. She works as a graphic designer and notes that her condition worsened after a cold caught at a crowded market in Noakhali. She has a comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies chest pain, hemoptysis, or fever. Physical examination reveals an oxygen saturation of SpO2 91%, BP 117/74 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 59 kg. Auscultation reveals bilateral expiratory wheezes and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up is in 1 week, or sooner if her breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Salma Begum, 62, female. Mrs. Begum returns for a follow-up visit, complaining of a creaking knee and joint stiffness in the morning that lasts for a few minutes. She is a retired civil servant and reports that her knee symptoms became worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Cox's Bazar. She has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. She denies any sudden locking of the joint, fever, or radiating back pain. On examination, her BMI 31.2, BP 147/92 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, and weight 86 kg. There is palpable crepitus in the right knee with mild joint line tenderness. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Sabbir Faruque, 64, male. Mr. Faruque presents for his first visit complaining of a spinning sensation and dizziness when looking up, which is accompanied by mild nausea. He works as a tailor and notes that these symptoms began after bumping his head on a rickshaw hood in Tejgaon. He denies any hearing loss, tinnitus, or focal weakness. Physical examination reveals Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, which reproduces transient rotary nystagmus. His other vitals are BP 118/81 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, and weight 88 kg. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up is in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Mahbub Ahmed, 41, male. Mr. Ahmed returns for a follow-up visit regarding his gastrointestinal symptoms. He presents with an atypical pattern of urgent loose stools every morning with little pain, though his general symptoms switch between loose and hard stools and worsen significantly with stress. He is a farmer by training but notes his symptoms became worse since starting a high-pressure job in Uttara. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies any blood in his stool, fever, or weight loss. On examination, his pain score 5/10, BP 140/88 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, and weight 84 kg. His abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 02:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Jui Mahmud, 27, female. Mrs. Mahmud returns for a follow-up on her dermatological condition, complaining of a ring-shaped itchy red rash with spreading edges, with the itching feeling much worse in humid weather. She is a homemaker and reports that the skin lesions originally began during the humid monsoon in Sylhet. She denies any joint pain, fever, or use of new body lotions. On examination, the affected area about 9 cm across is visible on her trunk, displaying active, scaling borders. Her other vitals are BP 125/82 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, and weight 44 kg. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the skin dry, not share towels, and wash clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 03:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Imtiaz Patwary, 75, male. Mr. Patwary presents for a detailed follow-up consultation to evaluate his worsening respiratory status. He has been experiencing a significant, acute flare-up of wheezing on walking and a marked increase in shortness of breath over the past week, which is compounding his long-standing history of heavy smoking. He is a tailor by profession and states that his breathing deteriorated dramatically after rubbish was burned near his home in Cox's Bazar. He reports that the smoke was thick and immediately triggered severe coughing fits, which left him feeling exhausted and unable to catch his breath. He has been struggling to perform his daily work at his sewing machine due to this exertion-induced breathlessness and has had to take multiple breaks. He denies having any high-grade fever, chills, purulent green or blood-tinged sputum, or chest pain that radiates to his arm or jaw. He also reports no orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. On physical examination, the patient appears to be in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing his accessory muscles of respiration during quiet breathing. His vital signs are recorded as SpO2 87% on room air, BP 110/85 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, and weight 85 kg. Chest auscultation reveals diminished breath sounds globally, with prominent, diffuse expiratory wheezes and coarse crackles bilaterally. There is no evidence of pedal edema, and his jugular venous pressure is not elevated. Heart sounds are distant but regular, with no murmurs detected. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was extensively counselled on the absolute necessity to stop smoking completely to prevent further irreversible lung damage. He was also advised to strictly avoid exposure to cooking smoke and environmental pollutants, and to ensure he takes the yearly flu vaccine to reduce the risk of future severe respiratory infections. He is instructed to monitor his symptoms closely and return for a follow-up in 1 week, or sooner if his breathing worsens or if he experiences chest pain.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Lipi Hossain, 66, female. Mrs. Hossain presents for her first visit, reporting a stiff shoulder for weeks, being unable to raise her arm, and being unable to reach behind her back. She is a retired civil servant and explains that these symptoms began gradually after a long illness in Jatrabari. She denies any history of trauma, neck pain, or numbness in her fingers. On physical examination, her shoulder lifts only to 70 degrees in abduction, and both active and passive range of motion are severely restricted. Other vitals are BP 112/77 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, and weight 61 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 03:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Anwar Molla, 50, male. Mr. Molla returns for a follow-up visit regarding his thyroid condition. He continues to report feeling slow and tired, along with weight gain and always feeling cold. He is an electrician and first noticed these changes when colleagues in Narayanganj remarked on his weight gain. He denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or changes in bowel habits. On examination, his TSH 10.2 mIU/L, BP 133/70 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, and weight 66 kg. No thyroid nodules or pretibial myxedema are present. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up is in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-06-17 03:30 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Aminul Molla, 43, male. Mr. Molla presents for his first visit, complaining of muffled hearing, a blocked ear after a cold, and a mild fever. He works as a police constable and reports that these symptoms began after a cold during a trip to Wari. He has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies any dizziness, tinnitus, or neck stiffness. On examination, his temperature is 100.0°F, BP 138/88 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, and weight 84 kg. Otoscopy of the affected ear reveals an erythematous, bulging tympanic membrane with loss of light reflex. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep the ear dry and not insert cotton buds. Follow-up in 1 week.
